def frames_and_history(state_lag,action_lag):

 for row in output_rows:
  s=row-state_lag;arow=row-action_lag

  gravity=g*(2*w*w-1)-2*w*np.cross(q,g)+2*q*np.dot(q,g)
  qrel=p32[s,:10]-default;qrel[8:]=0
  prev=np.zeros(10,np.float32) if row==output_rows[0] else recorded_raw[arow]
  frame=np.concatenate([gyro[s].astype(np.float32)*.25,gravity,cmd[s].astype(np.float32),qrel,v32[s,:10]*.05,prev]).astype(np.float32)
  frames.append(frame)
 frames=np.stack(frames)
 h=np.stack([frames[np.maximum(0,np.arange(k-9,k+1))] for k in range(len(frames))])
 assert np.isfinite(h).all() and np.max(np.abs(h))<100
 return torch.from_numpy(h)

Replay alignments are predeclared common approximations, not fitted timing estimates.
Autograd and frozen-input counterfactuals describe a policy response on recorded states, not feedback-loop gain or root cause.
